samples.scenario: Prediction target period: from 2023-05-16 to 2023-05-31. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Data released by the World Steel Association on April 21, 2023, showed that U.S. crude steel production totaled 6.7 million tonnes in March 2023, a 2.1% decrease compared to March 2022. [1, 5] For the first quarter of 2023, U.S. steel production was 19.4 million tonnes, representing a 4.0% decrease from the same period in 2022. This downward trend in steel production, a key manganese-consuming sector, offers a direct indication of manganese demand. <2> On February 24, 2023, the American Iron and Steel Institute (AISI) reported that based on preliminary Census Bureau data, the U.S. imported 2.61 million net tons of steel in January 2023. [1] This figure represented a 14.4% decrease compared to the same period in January 2022. [1, 2] As steel production is the primary consumer of manganese, a significant change in steel import volumes can influence domestic steel production and, in turn, affect the demand for manganese. <3> On January 31, 2023, the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) released its Mineral Commodity Summaries 2023 report, which provided a comprehensive overview of nonfuel mineral industry data for the 2022 calendar year. [1, 3] The manganese chapter of the report detailed that global steel production, the primary application for manganese, had decreased in 2022. Despite this, total U.S. imports of manganese, on a contained-weight basis, were estimated to have increased by nearly 20% in 2022 compared to 2021. [8] The leading suppliers of manganese ore to the U.S. from 2018–2021 were Gabon (67%), South Africa (19%), and Mexico (12%). [8] The report is the U.S. government's earliest comprehensive publication of 2022 mineral production data for the world, covering more than 90 individual commodities. [1, 3] <4> In an analysis published on January 20, 2023, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence predicted that 2023 would be a pivotal year for the automotive industry to secure manganese supplies for electric vehicle batteries. This forecast was influenced by the growing impact of the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), which encourages the development of a domestic battery supply chain in the United States. The IRA provides incentives for non-Chinese production, aiming to reduce reliance on China and tighten the supply pool for U.S. battery producers. The analysis underscored that meeting U.S. demand for manganese sulphate would be impossible without establishing new, non-Chinese sources, necessitating significant expansion in processing capacity outside of China for EVs to qualify for full tax credits.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> The Henderson City Council voted 4-0 on November 21, 2023, to approve a development project at the site of the former Three Kids Mine, with Mayor Michelle Romero being absent from the meeting. This defunct open-pit manganese mine, which operated from 1917 to 1961, is slated for a major transformation. The project, led by developers Lakemoor Ventures LLC and Pulte Homes, includes the environmental cleanup of contaminated soil containing substances like arsenic and lead. Following the remediation, a new community featuring 3,000 homes will be constructed on the site. The cleanup is anticipated to begin in 2024, with the first phase of the housing project expected to have a grand opening by early 2026. <2> A market analysis by the World Steel Association, published in its Short Range Outlook in October 2023, predicted that global steel demand would grow by 1.9% in 2024. [9] This forecast has a direct impact on manganese, as it is a key component in steel production. [10] The analysis also correctly noted that government initiatives, such as the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, are designed to bolster the supply of critical minerals like manganese by encouraging the development of manganese sulfate projects outside of China, particularly for the electric vehicle battery sector. [6, 7, 12] However, it was anticipated that significant new production from these projects would not come online until 2026/2027. [1, 3] <3> In its August 2023 mineral industry survey, the U.S. Geological Survey reported that U.S. imports of manganese ore experienced a significant decline to 475 metric tons, a sharp drop from 42,100 metric tons in July 2023. [3] The survey also noted that average spot prices for manganese ore delivered to China were 3% lower than in July 2023 and 23% lower than in August 2022. [3] Coinciding with these market changes, a military coup occurred in Gabon on August 30, 2023. [3, 5] Gabon is the world's second-largest producer of manganese. [3, 5] Following the coup, the leading manganese producer in the country, Eramet Group, temporarily suspended its operations on August 30 but resumed production the next day. [3] <4> Data released by the World Steel Association on April 21, 2023, showed that U.S. crude steel production totaled 6.7 million tonnes in March 2023, a 2.1% decrease compared to March 2022. [1, 5] For the first quarter of 2023, U.S. steel production was 19.4 million tonnes, representing a 4.0% decrease from the same period in 2022. This downward trend in steel production, a key manganese-consuming sector, offers a direct indication of manganese demand. <5> On February 24, 2023, the American Iron and Steel Institute (AISI) reported that based on preliminary Census Bureau data, the U.S. imported 2.61 million net tons of steel in January 2023. [1] This figure represented a 14.4% decrease compared to the same period in January 2022. [1, 2] As steel production is the primary consumer of manganese, a significant change in steel import volumes can influence domestic steel production and, in turn, affect the demand for manganese. <6> On January 31, 2023, the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) released its Mineral Commodity Summaries 2023 report, which provided a comprehensive overview of nonfuel mineral industry data for the 2022 calendar year. [1, 3] The manganese chapter of the report detailed that global steel production, the primary application for manganese, had decreased in 2022. Despite this, total U.S. imports of manganese, on a contained-weight basis, were estimated to have increased by nearly 20% in 2022 compared to 2021. [8] The leading suppliers of manganese ore to the U.S. from 2018–2021 were Gabon (67%), South Africa (19%), and Mexico (12%). [8] The report is the U.S. government's earliest comprehensive publication of 2022 mineral production data for the world, covering more than 90 individual commodities. [1, 3] <7> In an analysis published on January 20, 2023, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence predicted that 2023 would be a pivotal year for the automotive industry to secure manganese supplies for electric vehicle batteries. This forecast was influenced by the growing impact of the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA), which encourages the development of a domestic battery supply chain in the United States. The IRA provides incentives for non-Chinese production, aiming to reduce reliance on China and tighten the supply pool for U.S. battery producers. The analysis underscored that meeting U.S. demand for manganese sulphate would be impossible without establishing new, non-Chinese sources, necessitating significant expansion in processing capacity outside of China for EVs to qualify for full tax credits.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> In the second quarter of 2024, global manganese ore prices surged significantly due to major supply disruptions. The primary catalyst was the suspension of operations at South32's Groote Eylandt Mining Company (GEMCO) in Australia, one of the world's largest manganese producers, starting on March 18, 2024. [2, 5] The shutdown was forced by severe structural damage to port infrastructure caused by Tropical Cyclone Megan. [4, 5] The market situation intensified on April 21, 2024, when South32 announced the suspension could last until the first quarter of 2025. [2] This prolonged outlook created a tightening market circulation and prompted some miners and sellers at ports to halt sales quotes. [7] The supply concerns, coupled with increased demand from alloy plants, drove a sharp increase in spot prices for seaborne and port-side manganese ore through April. [7] <2> In a January 2024 forecast, analysts predicted that manganese ore prices would see a moderate rise to approximately $520 per tonne in 2024 before declining in the fourth quarter to around $495 per tonne. [2] This Q4 price was projected to be an 8% increase compared to the same period in 2023. [2] The outlook for the manganese market in 2024 is considered relatively favorable, though with a limited potential for an upturn. [2] Market dynamics are heavily reliant on China's economy and the global steel industry, with the World Steel Association forecasting a 1.9% growth in global steel demand for 2024. [2, 3] Other analysts expect ore prices to face pressure in 2024 due to uncertainty in China's steel and construction sectors. [3] Factors influencing the market include logistical challenges in major producer South Africa and the increasing use of manganese in electric vehicle batteries. [2, 3] By the fourth quarter of 2024, high port stocks and procurement of lower-priced ore by alloy plants were expected to cause prices to fluctuate downward. [4] <3> The Henderson City Council voted 4-0 on November 21, 2023, to approve a development project at the site of the former Three Kids Mine, with Mayor Michelle Romero being absent from the meeting. This defunct open-pit manganese mine, which operated from 1917 to 1961, is slated for a major transformation. The project, led by developers Lakemoor Ventures LLC and Pulte Homes, includes the environmental cleanup of contaminated soil containing substances like arsenic and lead. Following the remediation, a new community featuring 3,000 homes will be constructed on the site. The cleanup is anticipated to begin in 2024, with the first phase of the housing project expected to have a grand opening by early 2026. <4> A market analysis by the World Steel Association, published in its Short Range Outlook in October 2023, predicted that global steel demand would grow by 1.9% in 2024. [9] This forecast has a direct impact on manganese, as it is a key component in steel production. [10] The analysis also correctly noted that government initiatives, such as the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, are designed to bolster the supply of critical minerals like manganese by encouraging the development of manganese sulfate projects outside of China, particularly for the electric vehicle battery sector. [6, 7, 12] However, it was anticipated that significant new production from these projects would not come online until 2026/2027. It is important to note that subsequent forecasts issued in 2024 have since revised the steel demand growth projection downwards due to persistent economic headwinds. [1, 3] <5> In its August 2023 mineral industry survey, the U.S. Geological Survey reported that U.S. imports of manganese ore experienced a significant decline to 475 metric tons, a sharp drop from 42,100 metric tons in July 2023. [3] The survey also noted that average spot prices for manganese ore delivered to China were 3% lower than in July 2023 and 23% lower than in August 2022. [3] Coinciding with these market changes, a military coup occurred in Gabon on August 30, 2023. [3, 5] Gabon is the world's second-largest producer of manganese. [3, 5] Following the coup, the leading manganese producer in the country, Eramet Group, temporarily suspended its operations on August 30 but resumed production the next day. [3] <6> Data released by the World Steel Association on April 21, 2023, showed that U.S. crude steel production totaled 6.7 million tonnes in March 2023, a 2.1% decrease compared to March 2022. [1, 5] For the first quarter of 2023, U.S. steel production was 19.4 million tonnes, representing a 4.0% decrease from the same period in 2022. This downward trend in steel production, a key manganese-consuming sector, offers a direct indication of manganese demand. <7> On February 24, 2023, the American Iron and Steel Institute (AISI) reported that based on preliminary Census Bureau data, the U.S. imported 2.61 million net tons of steel in January 2023. [1] This figure represented a 14.4% decrease compared to the same period in January 2022. [1, 2] As steel production is the primary consumer of manganese, a significant change in steel import volumes can influence domestic steel production and, in turn, affect the demand for manganese. <8> On January 31, 2023, the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) released its Mineral Commodity Summaries 2023 report, which provided a comprehensive overview of nonfuel mineral industry data for the 2022 calendar year. [1, 3] The manganese chapter of the report detailed that global steel production, the primary application for manganese, had decreased in 2022. Despite this, total U.S. imports of manganese, on a contained-weight basis, were estimated to have increased by nearly 20% in 2022 compared to 2021. [8] The leading suppliers of manganese ore to the U.S. from 2018–2021 were Gabon (67%), South Africa (19%), and Mexico (12%). [8] The report is the U.S. government's earliest comprehensive publication of 2022 mineral production data for the world, covering more than 90 individual commodities. [1, 3] <9> In an analysis published on January 20, 2023, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence predicted that 2023 would be a pivotal year for the automotive industry to secure manganese supplies for electric vehicle batteries. The IRA provides incentives for non-Chinese production, aiming to reduce reliance on China and tighten the supply pool for U.S. battery producers. [2, 4] Most products from both countries were subjected to a 25% tariff. [2] However, a lower tariff of 10% was applied to Canadian energy products. [2, 3] An exemption for potash also applied; on March 7, 2025, the tariff on potash from Mexico and Canada was lowered to 10% for products not qualifying for preferential treatment under the USMCA. [4, 6] This trade policy could potentially impact the cost of manganese and manganese-containing products, as they are not listed among the exempted goods. The initial executive orders for the tariffs were signed on February 1, 2025, but a one-month delay was negotiated, pushing the effective date to March. [1] <2> The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) released its "Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025" report, with the manuscript approved for publication on January 31, 2025. [8, 10] This annual report is the earliest comprehensive government publication of global mineral production data for the year 2024. [2, 5] The summary provides a detailed overview of more than 90 nonfuel minerals and materials, covering domestic industry structure, government programs, tariffs, and five-year salient statistics. [2, 5] Specifically for manganese, the report indicates that global mine production saw a slight increase compared to 2023. [9] It also highlights the United States' reliance on other countries for its manganese supply, identifying the primary import sources for manganese ore between 2020 and 2023 as Gabon (63%), South Africa (23%), and Mexico (13%). [9] <3> In response to supply chain vulnerabilities, the United States accelerated investments in manganese refining facilities during the latter part of 2024. This strategic initiative, aimed at securing the domestic supply chain for electric vehicle (EV) batteries and reducing reliance on China, included significant funding for high-purity manganese sulfate (HPMSM) production. Key investments included a $20 million grant to South32’s Hermosa project in May 2024 and a $166 million grant to Element 25 in September 2024. <4> In the third quarter of 2024, an increase in manganese ore arrivals at Chinese ports, coupled with low acceptance of high-priced ore from downstream alloy plants facing severe losses, led to a downward fluctuation in spot prices and slow destocking of port inventories. Automakers are progressively adopting manganese-rich battery chemistries, such as lithium manganese iron phosphate (LMFP), to lower costs and decrease reliance on nickel and cobalt. [1] While the growing demand from the EV battery sector is significant, the steel industry remains the primary consumer of manganese. [2, 3] Analysts note that although the volume of manganese used in EV supply chains is currently small, it is expected to grow, while demand from the steel sector may decline over time. [3] The narrative around manganese is heavily focused on its use in EV batteries, partly due to its concentration in China's processing supply chain and companies seeking financing. [2, 3] Projections indicate that manganese demand for green energy applications is expected to rise. [1] This market condition was attributed to a combination of weak domestic demand and an increase in import volumes. [1] Major producers were affected, with both U.S. Steel and Nucor issuing guidance for the fourth quarter that anticipated significantly lower profits, and in the case of U.S. Steel, a potential loss. [1, 2] On December 19, 2024, U.S. Steel specifically guided for an adjusted loss per share, citing depressed steel prices, weak demand, and costs related to its new Big River 2 mill. [2] The broader market softness also impacted demand for key alloying elements such as manganese, which saw oversupply and price volatility throughout 2024 due to reduced purchasing from the steel sector. [3, 7] <7> According to data from the American Iron and Steel Institute (AISI), U.S. steel mills shipped 6,987,092 net tons in October 2024, a 4.9% decrease from the 7,346,373 net tons shipped in October 2023. Shipments in October 2024 also represented a 1.4% decline from the previous month, September 2024. Furthermore, U.S. raw steel production for the week ending December 7, 2024, was 1.668 million net tons. This marked a 2.2% decrease compared to the same period in the previous year, signaling weakened demand from manganese's primary consumer. The rules are designed to boost domestic production of clean energy property, including solar and wind components, inverters, battery components, and applicable critical minerals. A key clarification in the final rules modifies the definition of "production costs" to include the costs associated with the extraction of critical minerals. This change is intended to significantly incentivize investment in U.S. mining companies and domestic critical-mineral producers, ultimately strengthening the U.S. supply chain for these essential materials.

metadata.original_text: This time series records manganese CNY mtu data in the Commodity market price domain, with a collection frequency of daily, focusing on monitoring and analyzing relevant indicators. Prediction target period: from 2025-06-25 to 2025-07-10. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Operations at the Groote Eylandt Mining Company (GEMCO), one of the world's largest manganese producers, were suspended in March 2024 due to significant infrastructure damage caused by Tropical Cyclone Megan. The cyclone flooded mining pits and severely damaged the wharf and port infrastructure, leading to a halt in production and exports, which impacted the global manganese supply. An initial forecast for restarting shipments in the third quarter of 2024 was incorrect; the company later revised its timeline, expecting to recommence wharf operations and export sales in the first quarter of 2025 (Q3 FY25). Following an extensive recovery effort that involved over 317,000 hours of labor to rebuild the wharf, South32 officially announced the resumption of export sales on May 19, 2025. The first shipment of manganese ore departed from the newly reconstructed wharf on that day, with export volumes expected to ramp up through the June 2025 quarter and return to normal rates during the 2026 fiscal year. <2> A market trend report indicates a strategic shift in the electric vehicle (EV) battery sector towards Lithium-Manganese-Rich (LMR) chemistries, a technology being advanced by companies such as General Motors and LG Energy Solution. [1, 5] This battery chemistry is notable for its composition, using approximately 65% manganese and significantly less cobalt, which helps in reducing production costs. [1, 5] The LMR technology is reported to increase energy density by about 33% compared to Lithium Iron Phosphate (LFP) cells. [2, 5] This development is expected to be a major future driver for high-purity manganese demand in the United States, supporting domestic EV manufacturing. General Motors and LG Energy Solution plan to begin commercial production of these LMR prismatic battery cells by 2028. [2, 4] <3> A Q2 market report, published on May 7, 2025, detailed significant ongoing supply chain disruptions for U.S. manufacturers, analyzing market conditions as of April 30, 2025. The report identified an escalating tariff environment and shifts in production geographies as primary causes for these disruptions. It highlighted that the U.S. Manufacturing PMI fell to 48.7 in April, marking the second consecutive month of contraction and a five-month low. Consequently, rising factory-gate inflation was compelling component buyers to reassess their sourcing plans, impacting the import and pricing of raw materials. <4> A market report by John Zadeh, published on April 27, 2025, highlighted a significant price decline for manganese ore across major types and regions. The report attributes this downturn, which began in January 2025, to a combination of increased supply-side inventories and reduced demand from downstream alloy producers. It was also projected that market stabilization could potentially occur in the late second or early third quarter of 2025, possibly coinciding with seasonal increases in steel production. <5> In late April 2025, the electrolytic manganese metal (EMM) market, particularly in China, experienced a period of price stability. [2] Domestic EMM spot prices in China held steady at 13,350–13,550 yuan per metric ton, with the free-on-board (FOB) export price remaining at $1,870–$1,900/mt. [2] This stability was attributed to producers unifying to resist price reductions amid cautious purchasing from downstream buyers, such as stainless steel mills, which held lower than average inventories. [2] While Chinese FOB prices were stable, the global market showed regional differences: European buyers accepted premiums for guaranteed deliveries, Southeast Asian purchasers sought discounts for favorable payment terms, and North American buyers reduced their purchases to focus on domestic capacity. The initiative targets the Clarion–Clipperton Zone (CCZ), an area located in international waters between Mexico and Hawaii. This order focuses on securing a supply chain for battery metals, specifically manganese, nickel, copper, and cobalt, to reduce U.S. dependency on foreign mineral supplies and strategically counter China's industry dominance. The executive order also establishes a regulatory fast-track for deep-sea mining operations. <7> On April 15, 2025, the U.S. administration directed the Secretary of Commerce to initiate a Section 232 investigation into whether imports of processed critical minerals and their derivative products threaten national security. [1, 3, 4, 8] This probe specifically addresses concerns about U.S. reliance on foreign supply chains, particularly China's dominance in the processing of 30 out of 44 critical minerals. [2, 6] The investigation covers materials essential for electric vehicles, batteries, and defense applications. [2, 6] The Department of Commerce is tasked with delivering a report with findings and recommendations within 180 days, which could lead to the imposition of new tariffs, quotas, or other import restrictions to incentivize domestic production and reduce supply chain vulnerabilities. [3, 4] <8> An Executive Order titled 'Immediate Measures to Increase American Mineral Production' was issued on March 20, 2025. The order directs federal agencies to prioritize and expedite the permitting process for projects that can reduce United States' reliance on foreign mineral supplies. It also makes financial support available by delegating authority under the Defense Production Act (DPA) to the Secretary of Defense and the CEO of the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) to facilitate investment in domestic mineral production. Electric Metals USA responded to a separate, related Executive Order issued on April 15, 2025. That order initiated an investigation under Section 232 into national security risks from imported critical minerals, which Electric Metals USA stated enhances the strategic importance of its Emily Manganese Project in Minnesota. <9> On March 4, 2025, the U.S. government implemented tariffs on goods imported from Mexico and Canada. [2, 4] Most products from both countries were subjected to a 25% tariff. [2] However, a lower tariff of 10% was applied to Canadian energy products. [2, 3] An exemption for potash also applied; on March 7, 2025, the tariff on potash from Mexico and Canada was lowered to 10% for products not qualifying for preferential treatment under the USMCA. [4, 6] This trade policy could potentially impact the cost of manganese and manganese-containing products, as they are not listed among the exempted goods. The initial executive orders for the tariffs were signed on February 1, 2025, but a one-month delay was negotiated, pushing the effective date to March. [1] <10> The U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) released its "Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025" report, with the manuscript approved for publication on January 31, 2025. [8, 10] This annual report is the earliest comprehensive government publication of global mineral production data for the year 2024. [2, 5] The summary provides a detailed overview of more than 90 nonfuel minerals and materials, covering domestic industry structure, government programs, tariffs, and five-year salient statistics. [2, 5] Specifically for manganese, the report indicates that global mine production saw a slight increase compared to 2023. [9] It also highlights the United States' reliance on other countries for its manganese supply, identifying the primary import sources for manganese ore between 2020 and 2023 as Gabon (63%), South Africa (23%), and Mexico (13%). [9]
